launch-pa-pittsburgh-schenley-park.summary: A 456-acre Oakland park linking wooded trails, Panther Hollow, Flagstaff Hill, Schenley Plaza, sports facilities and Phipps Conservatory.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-schenley-park.hours: City park areas are generally open 6:00 a.m. to sunset when unlighted and until 11:00 p.m. where lighted. Phipps, the pool and golf course use separate schedules.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-schenley-park.parking: Parking is distributed among Schenley Plaza meters, Panther Hollow and Overlook drives, facility lots and Oakland streets. Route to the exact destination; university events change availability.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-schenley-park.arrival: Use Schenley Plaza for Phipps and the north end, Overlook Drive for the Oval and pool, or Panther Hollow Road for the lake and lower trails.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-schenley-park.restrooms: Dependable restrooms are inside Phipps and staffed recreation facilities during their hours; trail areas do not guarantee one.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-schenley-park.cost: Grounds, trails, plaza and overlooks are free. Phipps, golf, pool, rentals, food and events may cost separately.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-schenley-park.accessibility: The plaza and many facility approaches are paved, but the park is steep and wooded trails and Panther Hollow are uneven.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-schenley-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome outdoors but not in Phipps, pools, playground equipment or posted facilities.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-schenley-park.family: The plaza, Phipps, pool, Oval and slopes offer varied family stops, but choose one destination before arrival.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-schenley-park.transit: Frequent buses serve Oakland and Schenley Plaza; lower areas require a downhill walk and uphill return.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-schenley-park.need: Do not use one generic park pin. Pick Phipps, the plaza, Flagstaff Hill, Panther Hollow or the Oval first.

launch-pa-pittsburgh-frick-park.summary: Pittsburgh's largest historic regional park, with wooded ravines, the Environmental Center, Blue Slide Playground, fields, dog areas and Nine Mile Run trails.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-frick-park.hours: City park areas are generally open 6:00 a.m. to sunset when unlighted and until 11:00 p.m. where lighted. The Environmental Center keeps separate hours.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-frick-park.parking: Small free lots and curb spaces serve the Environmental Center, Blue Slide, fields and neighborhood trailheads; these are separate arrival zones.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-frick-park.arrival: Use the Environmental Center for maps. Blue Slide Playground and Nine Mile Run are reached from different park edges.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-frick-park.restrooms: Restrooms are most dependable at the Environmental Center and selected recreation facilities during open hours.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-frick-park.cost: Grounds, trails, playgrounds and ordinary center access are free; programs and reservations may cost separately.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-frick-park.accessibility: The center and nearby paths provide accessible options; ravine trails are hilly, muddy and not step-free.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-frick-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome outside signed off-leash areas. Keep dogs away from playgrounds and sensitive habitat.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-frick-park.family: Blue Slide, the Environmental Center, lawns and short nature walks work well for families.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-frick-park.transit: Buses serve Beechwood Boulevard and nearby streets; select a stop for the intended entrance.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-frick-park.need: Cell service and wayfinding can weaken in ravines. Download a map and avoid wet or icy slopes.

launch-pa-pittsburgh-point-state-park.summary: The downtown state park at the three-river confluence, centered on the fountain, fort remains, lawns, trails, Fort Pitt Museum and Block House.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-point-state-park.hours: Park grounds are open daily from sunrise to sunset. The paid Commonwealth Place lot is open 6:00 a.m.-11:00 p.m.; the museum, Block House, fountain and events keep separate schedules.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-point-state-park.parking: The Commonwealth Place lot is paid and limited. Downtown garages and transit are often easier; major events can close the lot and roads.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-point-state-park.arrival: Enter from Commonwealth Place or walk from downtown via the Portal Bridge. Allow extra time when an event controls access.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-point-state-park.restrooms: Restrooms are associated with staffed buildings during their hours; outdoor availability is not dependable after closing.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-point-state-park.cost: Grounds, fountain views, fort outlines and Block House are free. Parking and Fort Pitt Museum admission cost separately.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-point-state-park.accessibility: Broad paved promenades reach major areas, though event barriers and construction can change routes.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-point-state-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome outdoors but not in museum buildings.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-point-state-park.family: The fountain, river traffic and fort outlines make a compact family visit.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-point-state-park.transit: Downtown light rail and buses are within walking distance; riverfront trails connect from other shores.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-point-state-park.need: Large events can fully close or reconfigure the park, lot and riverfront paths. Check DCNR alerts.

launch-pa-pittsburgh-highland-park.summary: An East End park with formal gardens, reservoir loop, playgrounds, pool, courts, cycling track and the adjacent Pittsburgh Zoo.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-highland-park.hours: City park areas are generally open 6:00 a.m. to sunset when unlighted and until 11:00 p.m. where lighted. Pool and zoo schedules are separate.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-highland-park.parking: Free parking is spread around Reservoir Drive and recreation areas. Zoo visitors follow separate parking directions and fees.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-highland-park.arrival: Use the Highland Avenue entry for gardens and reservoir; route separately to the pool, track, playground or zoo.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-highland-park.restrooms: Facilities are most dependable at the pool, zoo and staffed recreation areas during open hours.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-highland-park.cost: Grounds, loop, gardens and playgrounds are free. Zoo, pool and programs may cost separately.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-highland-park.accessibility: The reservoir loop and main approaches are paved, though grades vary; the zoo has separate guidance.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-highland-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome in park areas but not inside the zoo or pool.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-highland-park.family: The super playground, pool, reservoir and zoo create a full family day; the zoo is a separate paid attraction.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-highland-park.transit: Buses serve Highland Avenue and the zoo area; choose the stop for the selected feature.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-highland-park.need: The reservoir is not a swimming area. Confirm seasonal pool hours and zoo tickets.

launch-pa-pittsburgh-riverview-park.summary: A steep wooded North Side park with Allegheny Observatory, visitor center, Chapel Shelter, pool, playground, overlooks and trails.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-riverview-park.hours: City park areas are generally open 6:00 a.m. to sunset when unlighted and until 11:00 p.m. where lighted. Observatory, center and pool use separate schedules.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-riverview-park.parking: Small free lots and curb spaces serve the center, observatory, pool and shelters.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-riverview-park.arrival: Choose the observatory, center, pool or trailhead before driving; the center is the best orientation point.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-riverview-park.restrooms: Restrooms are associated with the center, pool and reservable facilities during operating hours.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-riverview-park.cost: Grounds, trails, overlooks and playground are free; pool, programs and reservations may cost separately.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-riverview-park.accessibility: Developed facilities have paved approaches, but much of the park is steep with natural trails.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-riverview-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome outside the signed off-leash area.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-riverview-park.family: The pool, playground, center and short walks are family-friendly; longer trails can be steep and muddy.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-riverview-park.transit: Transit reaches nearby streets, but interior access is limited; verify the final uphill walk.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-riverview-park.need: The Observatory is not an always-open walk-in attraction. Reserve public tours when offered.

launch-pa-pittsburgh-emerald-view-park.summary: A Mount Washington network of overlooks, wooded hillsides, neighborhood parks, greenways and trails with iconic downtown views.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-emerald-view-park.hours: Park and overlook areas are generally open 6:00 a.m. to sunset when unlighted and until 11:00 p.m. where lighted. Use trails in daylight.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-emerald-view-park.parking: Grandview Avenue has limited curb parking; neighborhood parks and trailheads have separate small parking zones.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-emerald-view-park.arrival: Navigate to a named Grandview overlook for skyline views or a specific trailhead for hiking.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-emerald-view-park.restrooms: There is no dependable restroom at every overlook or trailhead; plan around open neighborhood facilities.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-emerald-view-park.cost: Overlooks, trails, playgrounds and park areas are free.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-emerald-view-park.accessibility: Grandview sidewalks and selected overlooks are paved; hillside trails are steep, narrow and uneven.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-emerald-view-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome; use caution on steep edges and clean up in residential areas.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-emerald-view-park.family: Overlooks and playgrounds are easy family stops; hillside hikes suit trail-ready children rather than strollers.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-emerald-view-park.transit: Inclines and Mount Washington buses reduce driving but still require a walk to individual destinations.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-emerald-view-park.need: This is not one contiguous lawn. Use named destinations and avoid steep muddy slopes after storms.

launch-pa-pittsburgh-mellon-park.summary: An East End park combining a historic walled garden with playground, seasonal spray park, tennis center, fields and public art.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-mellon-park.hours: City park areas are generally open 6:00 a.m. to sunset when unlighted and until 11:00 p.m. where lighted. Spray and tennis operations are seasonal.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-mellon-park.parking: Use curb parking on Beechwood, Fifth or Shady, observing restrictions. Entrances serve different park levels.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-mellon-park.arrival: Shady Avenue serves the garden and lower park; Beechwood and Fifth better serve some recreation areas.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-mellon-park.restrooms: Restrooms are most likely near staffed tennis or recreation facilities during their hours.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-mellon-park.cost: Park, gardens, playground, field and spray play are free; tennis programs may cost separately.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-mellon-park.accessibility: Major areas have paved approaches, but terraces, stairs and grades mean entrances are not equivalent.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-mellon-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome outside the spray park, playground, courts and garden beds.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-mellon-park.family: The playground, seasonal spray park and field pair well with the quieter walled garden.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-mellon-park.transit: Buses serve Fifth, Shady and nearby corridors; choose the stop closest to the entrance.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-mellon-park.need: The spray park is seasonal and weather-dependent. Verify operation and choose the right entrance for mobility needs.

launch-pa-pittsburgh-north-shore-riverfr.summary: A riverfront promenade linking PNC Park, Acrisure Stadium, water steps, public art, trails, docks, museums and downtown bridges.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-north-shore-riverfr.hours: Outdoor riverfront areas generally follow city park rules. Water steps, docks, museums and stadium grounds have separate schedules or closures.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-north-shore-riverfr.parking: Garages and lots are paid and event-priced. On game or concert days, reserve ahead or use transit.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-north-shore-riverfr.arrival: Choose PNC Park, Acrisure Stadium, Water Steps or Carnegie Science Center as the arrival anchor; walking from downtown is often simplest.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-north-shore-riverfr.restrooms: Dependable restrooms are inside staffed attractions during their hours; the open riverwalk does not guarantee late-night facilities.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-north-shore-riverfr.cost: Paths, lawns, Water Steps and public art are free. Parking, museums, events, cruises and food cost separately.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-north-shore-riverfr.accessibility: The main riverwalk is paved and mostly level, with ramps at key connections; events can alter routes.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-north-shore-riverfr.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome on ordinary paths but may be restricted near events and security zones.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-north-shore-riverfr.family: Water Steps, river traffic, public art and the science center make a strong family corridor; supervise beside water.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-north-shore-riverfr.transit: North Side light rail and buses serve the district; downtown bridges provide pedestrian access.
launch-pa-pittsburgh-north-shore-riverfr.need: Stadium schedules dominate parking, prices and closures. Check both venues and Water Steps operation before driving.
